Chain Rule 11: Cosine of Natural Logarithm

📘 English Note — 3-Tier Trigonometric-Logarithmic Chain Rule Formulation
The problem is a 3-tier composite function: y=f(g(h(x))),f(u)=cos⁡u,  u=g(v)=log⁡v,  v=h(x)=5xy = f(g(h(x))), \quad f(u) = \cos u, \; u = g(v) = \log v, \; v = h(x) = 5xy=f(g(h(x))),f(u)=cosu,u=g(v)=logv,v=h(x)=5x Applying Leibniz's 3-Tier Chain Rule: dydx=dydu⋅dudv⋅dvdx=[−sin⁡(log⁡5x)]⋅(15x)⋅(5)=−sin⁡(log⁡5x)x\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy}{du} \cdot \frac{du}{dv} \cdot \frac{dv}{dx} = [-\sin(\log 5x)] \cdot \left(\frac{1}{5x}\right) \cdot (5) = -\frac{\sin(\log 5x)}{x}dxdy​=dudy​⋅dvdu​⋅dxdv​=[−sin(log5x)]⋅(5x1​)⋅(5)=−xsin(log5x)​

Tier 2 (Middle) log⁡v\log vlogv ddv(log⁡v)=1v\frac{d}{dv}(\log v) = \frac{1}{v}dvd​(logv)=v1​

সম্মিলিত রূপ cos⁡(log⁡5x)\cos(\log 5x)cos(log5x) dydx=−1xsin⁡(log⁡5x)\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{1}{x}\sin(\log 5x)dxdy​=−x1​sin(log5x)
২. ধাপে ধাপে পূর্ণাঙ্গ গাণিতিক সমাধান
ধাপ ১:
উভয় পক্ষে xxx-এর সাপেক্ষে অন্তরীকরণ অপারেটর ddx\frac{d}{dx}dxd​ প্রয়োগ করি:
dydx=ddx[cos⁡(log⁡5x)]\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{d}{dx}\left[\cos(\log 5x)\right]dxdy​=dxd​[cos(log5x)]
ধাপ ২:

dydx=−sin⁡(log⁡5x)⋅ddx(log⁡5x)\frac{dy}{dx} = -\sin(\log 5x) \cdot \frac{d}{dx}(\log 5x)dxdy​=−sin(log5x)⋅dxd​(log5x)

dydx=−sin⁡(log⁡5x)⋅15x⋅ddx(5x)\frac{dy}{dx} = -\sin(\log 5x) \cdot \frac{1}{5x} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}(5x)dxdy​=−sin(log5x)⋅5x1​⋅dxd​(5x)

dydx=−sin⁡(log⁡5x)⋅55x=−sin⁡(log⁡5x)x\frac{dy}{dx} = -\sin(\log 5x) \cdot \frac{5}{5x} = -\frac{\sin(\log 5x)}{x}dxdy​=−sin(log5x)⋅5x5​=−xsin(log5x)​

Chain Rule 11: Engineering & Rigorous Analysis

Course: Mathematics-I (Differential Calculus) Theoretical Foundations & Examination Blueprint
⚠️ English Note — Critical AMIE Exam Traps & Pitfalls
  • Trap 1 (Missing Negative Sign of Cosine Derivative): The derivative of cos⁡(⋅)\cos(\cdot)cos(⋅) is −sin⁡(⋅)-\sin(\cdot)−sin(⋅). Forgetting the negative sign is a major error.
  • Trap 2 (Omitting Inner Linear Derivative 5): Differentiating log⁡(5x)\log(5x)log(5x) as only 15x\frac{1}{5x}5x1​ without multiplying by ddx(5x)=5\frac{d}{dx}(5x) = 5dxd​(5x)=5. Always demonstrate the complete 3-tier chain.
  • Trap 3 (Log Splitting Identity Verification): Note that log⁡(5x)=log⁡5+log⁡x  ⟹  ddx[log⁡(5x)]=0+1x=1x\log(5x) = \log 5 + \log x \implies \frac{d}{dx}[\log(5x)] = 0 + \frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{x}log(5x)=log5+logx⟹dxd​[log(5x)]=0+x1​=x1​, confirming the coefficient 555 cancels cleanly.
🟣 English Note — Domain, Positivity & Asymptotic Behavior (AMIE Rigor)
  • Positivity Requirement: For real log⁡(5x)\log(5x)log(5x), the argument must be strictly positive: 5x>0  ⟹  x>05x > 0 \implies x > 05x>0⟹x>0
  • Domain: Dom(y)=Dom(dydx)=(0,∞)\text{Dom}(y) = \text{Dom}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) = (0, \infty)Dom(y)=Dom(dxdy​)=(0,∞).
  • Asymptotic Behavior near Origin: As x→0+x \to 0^+x→0+, log⁡5x→−∞\log 5x \to -\inftylog5x→−∞. The sine oscillations have infinite frequency, and the amplitude multiplier −1x→−∞-\frac{1}{x} \to -\infty−x1​→−∞, producing unbounded oscillation.
💡 English Note — Substitution & Log-Splitting Proofs
Method A (3-Tier Leibniz Substitution): Let v=5x  ⟹  v′=5v = 5x \implies v' = 5v=5x⟹v′=5; u=log⁡v  ⟹  u′=15xu = \log v \implies u' = \frac{1}{5x}u=logv⟹u′=5x1​; y=cos⁡u  ⟹  y′=−sin⁡uy = \cos u \implies y' = -\sin uy=cosu⟹y′=−sinu. dydx=[−sin⁡(log⁡5x)]⋅(15x)⋅5=−sin⁡(log⁡5x)x\frac{dy}{dx} = [-\sin(\log 5x)] \cdot \left(\frac{1}{5x}\right) \cdot 5 = -\frac{\sin(\log 5x)}{x}dxdy​=[−sin(log5x)]⋅(5x1​)⋅5=−xsin(log5x)​ Method B (Logarithmic Expansion): y=cos⁡(log⁡5+log⁡x)  ⟹  dydx=−sin⁡(log⁡5+log⁡x)⋅(0+1x)=−sin⁡(log⁡5x)xy = \cos(\log 5 + \log x) \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = -\sin(\log 5 + \log x) \cdot \left(0 + \frac{1}{x}\right) = -\frac{\sin(\log 5x)}{x}y=cos(log5+logx)⟹dxdy​=−sin(log5+logx)⋅(0+x1​)=−xsin(log5x)​
